items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-21
items.q: I'll ask Mr. Eickward to read this, Jazz and Jazzism, which is an editorial that appeared in the New Orleans Times-Picayune, June of 20, 1918.

ctx.x: Let's see if it's working first. It sounds all right. Go ahead.

Look at me here. In 1918, the New Orleans papers, or the Times-Picayune, disowned us, and say that we were not from New Orleans. I'll ask Mr. Eickward to read this, Jazz and Jazzism, which is an editorial that appeared in the New Orleans Times-Picayune, June of 20, 1918. Mr. Eickward, would you please read that?

Jazz and Jazzism. Why is the jazz music, and therefore the jazz band? As well asked, why is the dime novel, or the grease-dripping doughnut? All are manifestations of a low streak in man's taste that has not yet come out in civilization's wash. Indeed, one might go farther, and say that jazz music is the indecent story, syncopated and counterpointed, like the improper anecdote.
